story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Create `/src/bet_bot/display/error_handler.py` module with error display logic 2. Implement `display_error(error: Exception, context: dict) -> str` function that formats errors for terminal 3. Implement categorization for error types: API, Network, Validation, Configuration, System 4. Implement user-friendly messages for each error category (not technical jargon) 5. Implement "contact support" information or documentation links where appropriate 6. Implement logging of full error details (stack trace, context) while showing simplified version to user 7. For API errors: show which API failed, suggested retry timing, documentation link 8. For network errors: show connection issue, suggest troubleshooting steps 9. For validation errors: show which field failed, expected format, example 10. For configuration errors: show missing configuration key, file location, setup instructions 11. For system errors: show error type, suggest environment/permission checks 12. Export `display_error()` from `/src/bet_bot/display/__init__.py`

doc.title: bet-bot Technical Specification
doc.section: Module Breakdown - Error Handling, System Architecture Flow
doc.snippet: Error Handling: If API-Football fails → use scrape backup. If scrape fails → continue with missing data (graceful degradation). Log all failures for debugging. Display errors in user-friendly way with actionable next steps.

doc.title: Story 7.1: Create Terminal Formatter for Picks
doc.snippet: Story 7.1 (done) establishes Rich library integration for terminal formatting. The formatter outputs colored tables with financial data. Error Display Handler (7.3) builds on this with error-specific formatting patterns.

doc.title: Story 7.2: Implement Results Renderer
doc.snippet: Story 7.2 (done) implements ERROR state rendering with message format: "❌ ANALYSIS FAILED" | error type | troubleshooting steps | logging location. Error Handler (7.3) provides the underlying display_error() function to support error state rendering.

doc.title: Exception Hierarchy Definition
doc.snippet: BetBotError (base) → APIError (APIAuthenticationError, APIRateLimitError, APINotFoundError, APIServerError), DataValidationError, DataStaleError, ScraperError, OpenAIError. Each exception includes context: url, status_code, response_body, field, value, reason, etc.

constraint.name: Exception Type Detection
constraint.description: Must handle exception types from: httpx (TimeoutException, ConnectError, NetworkError, HTTPStatusError), pydantic (ValidationError), built-ins (KeyError, ValueError, OSError, PermissionError, RuntimeError), and custom exceptions (APIError subclasses, DataValidationError, etc.)

constraint.name: API Key Sensitivity
constraint.description: NEVER log or display API keys in error messages. Use masked format (first 4 chars + "..." + last 4 chars) if API key is mentioned.

constraint.name: Logging Integration
constraint.description: Full error details (stack trace, context dict, system info) must be logged to ~/.bet-bot/logs/ with timestamp. User sees only simplified version in terminal. Log file path shown in error message.

constraint.name: User-Friendly Language
constraint.description: Error messages must use plain language without technical jargon. Include actionable next steps (retry timing, documentation links, file locations, troubleshooting steps) in each category.

constraint.name: Module Location
constraint.description: Error Handler module must be in /src/bet_bot/display/ directory, following naming pattern of formatter.py and renderer.py. File: error_handler.py

constraint.name: Return Type
constraint.description: display_error(error: Exception, context: dict | None = None) must return formatted error string, NOT print to console. Caller (CLI or renderer) decides when to print.

constraint.name: Error Categories
constraint.description: Exactly 5 categories: API, Network, Validation, Configuration, System. Each has dedicated formatter function (_format_api_error, _format_network_error, etc.) with category-specific guidance.

constraint.name: Rich Library Usage
constraint.description: Follow existing patterns from stories 7.1 (formatter) and 7.2 (renderer). Use Rich for: colored text ([green]/[red]), Panel for sections, emoji icons (❌, ⚠️, etc.). Consistent with project styling.

interface.name: display_error() Main Function
interface.signature: def display_error(error: Exception, context: dict | None = None) -> str
interface.description: Main entry point. Takes any exception and optional context dict. Returns formatted error message string. Detects error category and calls appropriate formatter (_format_api_error, _format_network_error, etc.).

interface.name: _categorize_error() Helper
interface.description: Detects error category by inspecting exception type and attributes. Returns: "api", "network", "validation", "configuration", "system", or "unknown".

interface.name: _format_api_error() Handler
interface.description: Formats API errors (APIError, APIAuthenticationError, APIRateLimitError, APIServerError, APINotFoundError, HTTPStatusError). Shows: which API failed, status code, suggested retry timing, documentation links.

interface.name: _format_network_error() Handler
interface.description: Formats network errors (TimeoutException, ConnectError, NetworkError). Shows: timeout duration or connection type, troubleshooting steps, API status links.

interface.name: _format_validation_error() Handler
interface.description: Formats validation errors (ValidationError, DataValidationError). Shows: field name, expected format, example valid value, type constraints.

interface.name: _format_config_error() Handler
interface.description: Formats config errors (KeyError for missing env vars, ValueError for invalid config). Shows: missing key name, .env file path, setup instructions, list of required/optional keys.

interface.name: _format_system_error() Handler
interface.description: Formats system errors (OSError, PermissionError, FileNotFoundError, RuntimeError). Shows: error type, affected file/directory, troubleshooting steps (permissions, disk space, etc.).

interface.name: _log_full_error() Logger
interface.signature: def _log_full_error(error: Exception, context: dict | None = None) -> str
interface.description: Logs full error details to ~/.bet-bot/logs/ with timestamp. Captures: stack trace, context dict, system info (Python version, OS, memory). Returns log file path for user notification.

interface.name: display/__init__.py Export
interface.description: Export display_error() for use by Story 8.1 (CLI integration) and Story 7.2 (renderer error state). Keep existing exports for formatter and renderer.

tests.standards: Error display uses pytest unit tests and integration tests with Rich library compatibility. Test patterns follow Story 7.1/7.2 conventions. Focus: exception type detection, message formatting (no crashes, proper string return), logging integration (file creation), security (no API keys in output).
tests.locations: /tests/unit/test_error_handler.py (unit tests for all display functions) /tests/integration/test_error_handler_integration.py (integration tests with real exceptions and logging)
tests.ideas:
- **Unit tests** (test_error_handler.py): - Display error main function with various exception types - Error categorization for all 5 categories (API, Network, Validation, Config, System) - API error formatting: each subtype (auth, rate limit, server, timeout) - Network error formatting: timeout vs connection refused vs DNS errors - Validation error formatting: Pydantic ValidationError, field extraction - Configuration error formatting: missing keys, setup instructions - System error formatting: permission errors, file not found, disk errors - Logging integration: verify log file created, full trace present, no API keys - Edge cases: None context, empty error message, missing error attributes - Output format: no exceptions raised, proper string return, Rich formatting preserved
- **Integration tests** (test_error_handler_integration.py): - Real exception objects from actual API failures (using fixtures) - Integration with renderer (error state calls display_error) - Full pipeline error scenarios (fetch fails, parse fails, API fails) - Context passing from different pipeline stages (source API, retry count) - Concurrent error handling (multiple errors in parallel) - Logging to actual ~/.bet-bot/logs/ with proper permissions
- **Coverage goal**: >90% code coverage of error_handler.py
